corpus.evidence: fixtures in the rule's own suite plus an adversarial wave; no vulnerable/safe corpus authored beside this record.

oracle.evidence: no independent decider for 'is this value a secret'. CodeQL's js/timing-attack is the nearest comparable analysis.

effectiveFp.evidence: not measured under the formal protocol. Corpus fell 42 -> 41 when the location tails landed, so the volume is too low here to sample n>=20 from this corpus alone.

reachability.evidence: the rule requires an UNTRUSTED SOURCE on one side — untrustedSources defaults to req/request/ctx/event — and reports only where that path resolves. Confirmed by the adversarial wave: `a.apiToken === b.apiToken` with no taint source is silent, `req.headers.token === user.apiToken` reports. `process` is deliberately absent from the source list, because in `req.headers['x-sig'] === process.env.SIGNING_KEY` the env read is the secret being protected, not the lever.

adversarial.evidence: a 9-case wave scored 9/9: five real secret comparisons (token, clientSecret, signature, signatureUrl, hmac) all report through an untrusted source, and four location tails (path, hostname, count, route) stay silent. `signatureUrl` is the deliberate one — a presigned URL carries its signature and IS the credential, which is why url/uri are excluded from the tails. UNMET until a second wave finds nothing new; this one found nothing, but it is the FIRST wave and the axis asks for a second.

realSource.evidence: measured on 8 pinned repositories; the location-tails fix was driven by Shopify/cli's OAuth callback server, where `requestUrl.pathname !== STORE_AUTH_CALLBACK_PATH` was a CWE-208 finding on a route.

partition.evidence: not probed against the other comparison rules.

knownGaps.summary: whether a value is a secret is decided from its identifier, so a secret with a neutral name is invisible.
knownGaps.why: without types there is nothing else to read; the untrusted-source requirement is what keeps this from being a name-only rule.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: the rule becomes type-aware, or a taint summary can label the value.

knownGaps.summary: DEFAULT_NON_SECRET_TAILS is a word list, and a project may name a real secret with one of those tails.
knownGaps.why: the list is documented, generated into the schema description, and REPLACEABLE via nonSecretTails — a consumer whose vocabulary differs can set their own.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: a corpus finding shows a real secret suppressed by a tail.

notes: Sealed 2026-08-21. `reachability` MET, which is 1 of 1 across all 97 records — the untrusted-source requirement is exactly what that axis asks for, and it is why the adversarial wave's first five cases were silent until the harness was corrected to include a taint source.
